study type: Secondary analysis of a prospective observational study
exposure: College education vs. no college education
outcome: Self-reported overall pain during postpartum hospitalization
cohort: 494 postpartum patients who used an oral opioid at least once during their postpartum hospitalization at a single institution from May 2017 to July 2019
finding: Psychosocial factors, particularly relationship status and employment status, which are indicators of social support, are associated with postpartum pain experience.
mod_finding: While the study does not examine mode of delivery as a primary focus, it notes that 84% of the participants underwent a cesarean delivery.
